title: Jaipur's Amber Terrace Named Among World's 25 Best New Hotel Restaurants
excerpt: Amber Terrace, the rooftop Pan-Asian lounge at The Leela Palace Jaipur, is the Indian entry on Travel + Leisure's ranking of the world's 25 best new hotel restaurants, chosen from 120 venues across 17 countries.
body:
• Amber Terrace at The Leela Palace Jaipur has been named to Travel + Leisure's list of the world's 25 best new hotel restaurants, the Indian entry on the ranking.
  • Travel + Leisure's experts selected 25 venues from 120 hotel restaurants and bars across 17 countries, including cruise ship and train dining halls.
  • The rooftop lounge pairs modern Asian cuisine with root-to-fruit cocktails inspired by the botanical traditions of Rajasthan's House of Vaid healers.
  • The honour caps a strong run for the palace hotel, which holds Two Michelin Keys and multiple Condé Nast Traveller awards.

Jaipur's Amber Terrace has taken its place among the world's finest hotel dining rooms. The rooftop cocktail bar and restaurant at The Leela Palace Jaipur has been named to Travel + Leisure's list of the world's 25 best new hotel restaurants — the Indian entry on a ranking drawn from 120 hotel restaurants and bars across 17 countries.

The list, compiled by Travel + Leisure's experts, spans the full spectrum of hotel dining, from classic fine-dining rooms to cruise ship and train dining halls. It places the Jaipur newcomer in the company of openings such as chef Marcus Samuelsson's eponymous restaurant at the Morrow Washington DC and a cocktail bar set in a field in upstate New York.

"Hotels have seriously upped their culinary game."

— Travel + Leisure

A rooftop rooted in Rajasthani botany

Amber Terrace is a rooftop Pan-Asian lounge overlooking the Aravalli hills, pairing modern Asian cuisine with a cocktail programme built around a root-to-fruit philosophy — using whole botanicals, from root to fruit, in every pour. The concept draws on the botanical heritage once nurtured by the House of Vaid, the traditional Rajasthani family of botanical healers, giving the bar a distinctly local anchor beneath its contemporary Asian menu.

The venue launched earlier this year, introduced around the finals of the Leela Polo Cup in February, and has moved quickly to establish itself. In July, the terrace hosted an exclusive one-night guest shift by Nouvelle Vague, a bar ranked among the World's 50 Best, built around craftsmanship, local botanicals and cultural storytelling — an early signal that the industry was paying attention.

A palace hotel on a winning streak

The recognition is the latest in a run of honours for The Leela Palace Jaipur. The 194-room palace, set across eight acres of landscaped gardens against the Aravalli Hills near Kookas, earned Two Michelin Keys in 2025. It has since been named among the top hotels in India by Condé Nast Traveller UK's Readers' Choice Awards, taken Favourite Indian Leisure Hotel at the Condé Nast Traveller India Readers' Travel Awards 2025, and collected Preferred Hotels & Resorts' 2026 Award of Excellence for Hotel Partner of the Year across India, the Middle East and Africa.

Its dining portfolio is deep: alongside Amber Terrace sit Jamavar, the group's royal-Indian fine dining restaurant set amid 3,50,000 hand-cut Thikri mirrors and 18-carat gold leafwork, the all-day Aravalli Dining Room, the Jharokha Bar and the Peacock Lounge. The T+L nod, though, is the first time one of its restaurants has been singled out on a global ranking.

Why hotel restaurants are having a moment

The list reflects a broader shift in where ambitious dining happens. Hotel restaurants, long treated as a safe fallback for travellers, are increasingly the site of the most daring openings: built-in footfall, lavish fit-outs and corporate backing let chefs take risks that standalone ventures often cannot afford. For India's luxury hotels, which have traditionally competed on service and setting, the kitchen — and the bar — has become the new battleground.

Jaipur, meanwhile, keeps strengthening its case as a serious dining destination rather than just a heritage stopover. A global endorsement in print gives the city's luxury hotel scene exactly the kind of validation that travels well beyond Rajasthan.

A natural stop for the diaspora circuit

For overseas Indians, the timing is convenient. Wedding season and the winter travel months bring thousands of diaspora visitors to Rajasthan each year, and Jaipur's palace hotels sit firmly on that circuit. A rooftop with a global ranking attached is one more reason to linger in the Pink City — and a useful answer to the perennial question of where to take visiting family for a memorable night out.

What's next

Travel + Leisure's ranking gives the hotel a powerful marketing hook heading into the peak winter season, when Jaipur's palace hotels run at their fullest. If Amber Terrace's trajectory so far — a February launch, a World's 50 Best bar collaboration by July, a global list by September — is any guide, the rooftop is just getting started.
